title: Score Based Error Correcting Code Decoder
claim: Decoding can be viewed as reversing a forward noising process, with a guided denoiser iteratively steering noisy observations back toward valid codewords.
layout: 2 heatmap panels left-to-right, with a loop module diagram below
description: The top half has two large square heatmap panels on a dark purple background with a yellow-green density. The left panel is labeled 'Forward diffusion'. Its white and cyan noisy trajectories start at +1 and −1 and spread out toward a dashed yellow hard-decision line at 0. An arrow labeled y leads to the right panel, 'Reverse PF-ODE decoding'. There, the smooth trajectories converge back to ±1 and the density concentrates at those two values. A long arrow above each panel shows the direction of the process. Below, a rounded yellow box holds a feedback loop. The noisy vector x^(i)=y and the syndrome s(x^(i)) feed the purple SB-ECC denoiser block, which outputs ε̂θ. A blue update block computes x^(i+1)=x^(i)−Δσ ε̂θ, and x^(i+1) loops back to the reverse panel. The eye goes first to the colorful heatmaps.
caption: Per-bit view of decoding as deterministic denoising. Left: forward corruption (channel as a forward diffusion): each curve is one coordinate $k$, where a clean BPSK symbol $x_{s,k}\in\{\pm1\}$ is perturbed into $y_k=x_{s,k}+z_k$ as the noise level increases. Right: reverse probability-flow ODE (PF-ODE) decoding: starting from $x_k^{(0)}=y_k$, the learned denoiser (with parity/\,syndrome guidance) drives each coordinate toward a valid codeword, concentrating mass back near $\pm1$. Background heatmaps depict empirical marginal density over coordinates, and the dashed line marks the hard-decision boundary at $0$.
abstract: Error-correcting codes enable reliable communication, yet practical soft decoding remains challenging across code families and block lengths. We propose SB-ECC, a score-based decoder that casts decoding as continuous-time denoising. A neural denoiser defines a probability-flow ordinary differential equation (ODE) that iteratively updates the noisy channel observation toward a valid codeword, guided by parity constraints. The model is trained across noise levels without time/SNR conditioning, enabling inference without SNR estimation and supporting a direct latency accuracy trade off controlled by the ODE solver budget. We use the raw signed channel observation as input for learning a continuous denoising field. Across 42 code/SNR settings, SB-ECC achieves the best BER in 39/42 entries, with an average SNR gain of 0.17dB and a maximum gain of 0.46dB over the strongest competing baseline, we showed that swapping the solver from Euler to DPM preserves -ln(BER) while reducing end-to-end decoding time by 8.86% on average (up to 12.82%).
